nodes.name: FeCoNi LDH molten salt synthesis
nodes.procedure: Typically, 20g KNO3 10g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O 10g Fe(NO3)3·9H2O and 10g Co(NO3)2·6H2O were added into a quartz crucible and then placed into a muffle furnace at 150°C. As the reagents became molten, the cleaned NF was placed in the crucible and immersed in molten salt for 7 min. Then the NF was taken out from the muffle furnace and naturally cooled to room temperature. Finally, the sample was washed with DI water and ethanol to remove the metal salt.

nodes.name: NiNi LDH molten salt synthesis
nodes.procedure: Different salts, including potassium nitrate and nickel nitrate hexahydrate containing bound water, are mixed to form metal salt mixtures that can melt at low temperatures. Then the mixed metal salt is added to a quartz crucible and heated in a muffle furnace to form a homogeneous molten salt solution at 150°C. After that, nickel foam is put into the solution for 7 min of reaction. Then, it was removed and cleaned to obtain a multi-level hierarchical array of NiNi LDH materials.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiNi LDH composed of uniformly arranged nanosheets with ~90 nm thickness on nickel foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a and Fig. 2b are the SEM and TEM images of NiNi LDH prepared at 7 min... composed of numerous uniformly arranged nanosheets with about 90 nm thickness on the nickel foam substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiNi LDH exhibits secondary regular array protrusions nanosheet structure with 10 nm thick curved/wrinkled secondary nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images clearly illustrate a secondary regular array protrusions nanosheet structure on the surface of the nanosheet. The secondary nanosheet exhibit a curved or wrinkled shape for the too thin thickness of about 10 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiNi LDH shows clear interplanar distance of 0.25 nm corresponding to (101) plane with many lattice distortions and dislocations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2c shows a typical HRTEM image of NiNi LDH. The clear interplanar distance of (101) plane of NiNi LDH is 0.25 nm. Besides, many lattice distortions and dislocations could be observed...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Ni and O in NiNi LDH nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping indicated the Ni, O existence and homogeneous distribution in overall NiNi LDH nanosheets (Fig. 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiNi LDH diffraction peaks at 12.8°, 25.8°, 35.5°, 42.4° assigned to (001), (002), (101), (102) planes (PDF#22-0752); broadened peaks indicate polycrystalline nature and defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both of them exhibited similar diffraction peaks located at 12.8°, 25.8°, 35.5°, and 42.4°, assigned to the (001), (002), (101) and (102) crystallographic planes of NiNi LDHs (PDF#22-0752), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows increased pre-edge intensity at ~8332 eV and positive white line shift in NiNi LDH indicating centrosymmetry breaking and defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2f shows the XANES of K-edge of Ni, indicating the increased intensity of pre-edge at about 8332 eV of NiNi LDH (shown in the right inset of Fig. 2f). The positive shift of white line of NiNi LDH is also shown...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS shows lower coordination numbers and slightly longer Ni-Ni bond length in NiNi LDH indicating abundant defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform (FT) of EXAFS (FT-EXAFS) curves justified the coordination numbers (CN) and bond lengths of Ni-Ni and Ni-O (Fig. 2g).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiNi LDH Ni 2p3/2 peaks: Ni²⁺ at 855.6 eV, Ni³⁺ at 856.9 eV (slightly higher than NiNi LDH-HT due to defects creating unsaturated coordination bonds).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectrum... shows the Ni2p3/2 peaks of Ni²⁺ and Ni³⁺ are situated in 855.6 eV and 856.9 eV, which is slightly higher than that of NiNi LDH-HT (855.6 eV and 856.7 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiNi LDH has Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 160.2 m²/g, higher than NiNi LDH-HT (60.5 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiNi LDH (160.2 m²/g) owns the higher Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface areas than NiNi LDH-HT (60.5 m²/g)...

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi LDH interplanar fringe distance of 0.26 nm assigned to (012) plane with defects and atomic distortions observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image in Fig. 3d exhibits the interplanar fringe with a distance of 0.26 nm, assigned to the (012) crystalline plane of FeCoNi LDH. Moreover, some defects and distortions of atoms also clearly were observed...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows even distribution of Fe, Co, Ni, O elements in FeCoNi LDH array.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the EDS mapping illustrated the Fe, Co, Ni, O element evenly distributed in the array (Fig. 3e).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi LDH metal molar ratio Fe:Co:Ni = 12.80:1.00:2.77 confirmed by ICP-OES.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-OES measurements show that the similar metal molar ratio of Fe, Co, and Ni are 12.80:1.00:2.77 and 12.70:1.00:2.84 for FeCoNi LDH and FeCoNi LDH-HT, respectively (Table S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi LDH similar crystalline structure to FeNi LDH (PDF#40-0215) with slight negative peak shift (enlarged interplanar spacing from Co incorporation) and broadened peaks (defects).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 3f, the XRD pattern of FeCoNi LDH and FeCoNi LDH-HT were evidenced owning a similar crystalline structure with FeNi LDH (PDF #40-0215). Especially, the diffraction peaks... show a slightly negative shift...

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi LDH shows Fe 2p3/2 and Ni 2p3/2 binding energy slightly blue shifted and O 1s slightly red shifted due to defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: But it still needs to note that the Fe 2p3/2 and Ni 2p3/2 binding energy is slightly blue shift while that of O 1s slightly red shift for the existence of defects.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi LDH exhibits specific surface area of 154.0 m²/g, higher than FeCoNi LDH-HT (71.3 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FeCoNi LDH and FeCoNi LDH-HT exhibited a specific surface area of 154.0 m²/g, 71.3 m²/g, respectively (Fig. S16).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi LDH Fe/Ni K-edge: white line indicates increased valence; reduced k³χ(k) oscillation amplitude; FT-EXAFS peak position/intensity changes; WT shows reduced Ni-M intensity indicating lower crystallization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3h, 4j, the white line shows the increased valence state... FT-EXAFS curves of Fe and Ni K-edge (Fig. 3i, 3k) show a similar peak position shift and intensity change... the weaker intensity of Ni-M in the FeCoNi LDH illustrates the reduced crystallization...

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNi LDH lattice fringes with 0.25 nm interlayer spacing attributed to (012) crystallographic plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM characterization further convicted the lattice fringes with an interlayer spacing of 0.25 nm, attributed to the (012) crystallographic plane of FeNi LDH (Fig. 6c).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo LDH lattice distance of 0.26 nm corresponding to (012) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image shows that the NiCo LDH lattice distance of the (012) plane is 0.26 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNi LDH and NiCo LDH confirmed as corresponding LDH phases (PDF#40-0215 and PDF#40-0216) with crystalline face spacings consistent with HRTEM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of as-prepared LDHs were confirmed as corresponding LDH phase FeNi LDH (PDF#40-0215) and NiCo LDH (PDF#40-0216) (Fig. 6i).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeNi LDH and NiCo LDH show chemical states similar to literature reports.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS results further show that the synthesized NiCo LDH and FeNi LDH are in a similar chemical state as reported in the literature (Fig. 6j, k, Fig. S24, S25).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiNi LDH by MSBWM shows conspicuous EPR bulge indicating unpaired electrons and defects, unlike hydrothermal NiNi LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy was applied... the sample prepared by MSBWM exhibited the conspicuous bulge. The results further illustrate the existence of the amount of defects.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNi LDH at 1.41 V: Eg=457 cm⁻¹, A1g=530 cm⁻¹ (Niᴵᴵ-O); weaker intensity, larger half-peak width vs LDH-HT (blue-shifted); faster NiOOH formation (peaks at 462/453 cm⁻¹ appear suddenly at 1.44 V).
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the applied voltage is 1.41 V, the Eg and A1g lattice mode are clearly well-defined at 457 cm⁻¹ and 530 cm⁻¹... Compared with the FeCoNi LDH, the Raman spectra of FeCoNi LDH-HT obviously shows the vibrations at 457 and 523 cm⁻¹... with the applied voltage increase to 1.44 V, the noticeable changes... verify the surface restructuration...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiNi LDH Cdl = 1.2 mF cm⁻² (higher than NiNi LDH-HT 0.35 mF cm⁻²) estimated from non-Faradaic CV at different scan rates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It clearly shows that the Cdl value of NiNi LDH is 1.2 mF cm⁻², higher than 0.35 mF cm⁻² of the NiNi LDH-HT.
